title: Who's driving your bill?
briefing: More about your power bill. Four posts. Some of them are mine. Maybe.

posts.body: While capacity charges currently account for approximately 15 to 20 percent of a typical customer's electric bill, they represent the single largest cost component that state utility commissions like the NJBPU cannot directly set, regulate, or change.
July vs July: NJ home electricity prices barely moved, 25.11¢ → 25.19¢ per kWh (EIA). The big jump was summer 2025.

quote.text: The fastest way to lower bills is getting new power generation built.
quote.speaker: Ben Hertz-Shargel, NJBPU President

posts.body: Atlantic City Electric's average monthly bills, for example, will rise by $4.09 because of changes to its Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative charges, certain infrastructure investments, and shifts in transmission charges set federally. But those same bills will fall by $4.14 due to changes to some Societal Benefits Charge components and lost sales related to energy efficiency and conservation programs, leaving the average monthly bill 5 cents cheaper than before.
